name: Pasta Carbonara
description: Authentic Roman pasta dish with eggs, cheese, guanciale, and black pepper.
instructions: Cook spaghetti in salted boiling water until al dente.
Fry guanciale until crispy.
Mix eggs with grated Pecorino and black pepper.
Combine hot pasta with guanciale, then mix with egg mixture off heat.
Serve immediately with extra cheese.
history: Carbonara originated in Rome after World War II, likely created by Italian charcoal workers (carbonari) or as a tribute to Allied soldiers with bacon and eggs.

name: Pizza Napoletana
description: Traditional Neapolitan pizza with San Marzano tomatoes, mozzarella, and fresh basil.
instructions: Stretch pizza dough by hand into a round shape.
Spread crushed San Marzano tomatoes evenly.
Add torn mozzarella pieces.
Bake in wood-fired oven at 485°C for 60-90 seconds.
Garnish with fresh basil and olive oil.
history: Pizza Napoletana dates back to 18th century Naples, originally food for the poor. The Margherita variant was created in 1889 honoring Queen Margherita.

name: Risotto alla Milanese
description: Creamy saffron-infused risotto from Milan, golden in color and rich in flavor.
instructions: Sauté onion in butter and marrow.
Toast rice, then deglaze with white wine.
Add warm broth gradually while stirring constantly.
Infuse saffron in broth and add halfway through cooking.
Finish with butter and Parmesan (mantecatura).
history: Created in 1574 during Milan Cathedral construction, legend says a apprentice added saffron to rice as a joke, creating this golden masterpiece.

name: Coq au Vin
description: Classic French braised chicken in red wine with mushrooms, bacon, and pearl onions.
instructions: Brown chicken pieces and bacon separately.
Sauté vegetables in bacon fat.
Deglaze with wine and add herbs.
Braise chicken slowly for 1.5 hours until tender.
Reduce sauce and serve with crusty bread.
history: Ancient Gallic dish dating to Roman times, traditionally made with rooster. Julia Child popularized it internationally in the 1960s.

name: Bouillabaisse
description: Traditional Provençal fish stew with various Mediterranean fish, saffron, and rouille.
instructions: Prepare fish stock with bones and aromatics.
Layer fish by cooking time in seasoned broth.
Add saffron and tomatoes.
Simmer gently until fish is cooked.
Serve with rouille-spread croutons.
history: Originated from Greek settlers in Marseille 2600 years ago. Originally fishermen's soup made from bony rockfish unsellable at market.

name: Paella Valenciana
description: Authentic Valencian paella with rabbit, chicken, snails, green beans, and saffron.
instructions: Sauté meat in paella pan until golden.
Add vegetables and cook briefly.
Add rice, saffron-infused broth, and rosemary.
Cook without stirring for 18 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes before serving.
history: Born in Albufera wetlands near Valencia in 18th century. Farmers and laborers cooked rice with available ingredients over open fire.

name: Gazpacho Andaluz
description: Cold tomato soup from Andalusia, refreshing summer staple with raw vegetables.
instructions: Soak bread in water.
Blend all vegetables with soaked bread.
Emulsify with olive oil and vinegar.
Strain for smooth texture.
Chill thoroughly before serving.
history: Pre-Roman origins, originally garlic, bread, oil and vinegar. Tomatoes added after Columbian Exchange. Essential for surviving Andalusian summers.

name: Sauerbraten
description: German pot roast marinated in vinegar and wine, served with red cabbage and dumplings.
instructions: Marinate beef 3-5 days in spiced vinegar-wine mixture.
Brown meat and sauté marinade vegetables.
Braise slowly for 2-3 hours.
Thicken sauce with crushed gingerbread.
Serve with potato dumplings and red cabbage.
history: Medieval preservation method evolved into delicacy. Each German region has variations. Essential dish for Sunday family dinners.

name: Moussaka
description: Layered eggplant casserole with spiced meat sauce and creamy béchamel topping.
instructions: Slice and salt eggplants, then fry.
Prepare meat sauce with tomatoes and spices.
Make béchamel sauce with milk and flour.
Layer eggplant, meat, repeat, top with béchamel.
Bake until golden brown on top.
history: Modern version created by chef Nikolaos Tselementes in early 1900s, adding French béchamel to traditional Ottoman dish.

name: Bacalhau à Brás
description: Portuguese codfish dish with scrambled eggs, potatoes, and olives.
instructions: Desalt codfish for 24-48 hours, changing water.
Shred cod and fry with onions.
Add matchstick potatoes and fry until golden.
Pour beaten eggs and scramble gently.
Garnish with olives and parsley.
history: Portugal's national dish with over 1001 preparations. Bacalhau sustained Portuguese during Age of Discoveries and maritime explorations.

name: Tiramisù
description: Classic Italian dessert with coffee-soaked ladyfingers and mascarpone cream.
instructions: Brew strong espresso and let cool.
Whip egg yolks with sugar, add mascarpone.
Fold in whipped egg whites.
Dip ladyfingers briefly in coffee and layer.
Spread mascarpone cream, repeat layers, dust with cocoa.
history: Created in Treviso in the 1960s, possibly at Restaurant Le Beccherie. Name means 'pick me up' referring to caffeine and energy boost.

name: Osso Buco
description: Braised veal shanks with vegetables, white wine, and gremolata.
instructions: Dredge veal shanks in flour and brown.
Sauté vegetables (soffritto).
Deglaze with wine, add broth and tomato paste.
Braise for 2 hours until meat is fork-tender.
Top with gremolata before serving.
history: Traditional Milanese dish dating to 19th century. Originally humble food, now considered haute cuisine. Traditionally served with risotto alla milanese.

name: Ratatouille
description: Provençal vegetable stew with eggplant, zucchini, peppers, and tomatoes.
instructions: Salt and drain eggplant slices.
Sauté each vegetable separately.
Prepare tomato sauce with garlic and herbs.
Layer vegetables in tomato sauce.
Simmer gently until all vegetables are tender.
history: Peasant dish from Nice, originally called 'ratatouille niçoise'. Gained international fame through Pixar's 2007 animated film.

name: Crêpes Suzette
description: Thin French pancakes flambéed with orange butter sauce and Grand Marnier.
instructions: Make thin crêpe batter and cook in buttered pan.
Prepare orange butter sauce with juice and zest.
Fold crêpes and warm in sauce.
Add Grand Marnier and flambé tableside.
Serve immediately while flaming.
history: Created accidentally in 1896 by young waiter Henri Charpentier for Prince of Wales. Flaming presentation became theatrical restaurant tradition.

name: Tortilla Española
description: Spanish potato omelette, national dish served hot or cold.
instructions: Slice potatoes thinly and fry gently in olive oil.
Sauté onion until soft.
Beat eggs and mix with potatoes and onion.
Cook in pan, flip using plate technique.
Serve slightly runny or fully set per preference.
history: Originated in Navarre during Carlist Wars (1830s) as hearty meal for soldiers. Debate continues about adding onion - purists say yes.

name: Pulpo a la Gallega
description: Galician-style octopus with paprika, salt, and olive oil on wooden plate.
instructions: Freeze octopus beforehand to tenderize.
Boil octopus with bay leaf until tender (45 min).
Slice into medallions.
Arrange over boiled potato slices.
Season with paprika, salt, and generous olive oil.
history: Ancient Celtic tradition in Galicia. Octopus tentacles represent pilgrimage paths to Santiago. Served on wooden plates (queiroga).

name: Wiener Schnitzel
description: Breaded and fried veal cutlet, crispy golden exterior with tender meat.
instructions: Pound veal very thin between plastic wrap.
Dredge in flour, dip in beaten eggs, coat with breadcrumbs.
Fry in clarified butter until golden on both sides.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve immediately with lemon wedge and parsley potatoes.
history: Despite name meaning 'Viennese', origins debated between Austria and Germany. Became symbol of Central European cuisine in 19th century.

name: Käsespätzle
description: German egg noodles with melted cheese and crispy fried onions.
instructions: Mix flour, eggs, salt into thick batter.
Press through Spätzle maker into boiling water.
Drain when noodles float.
Layer with grated cheese, bake until melted.
Top with caramelized fried onions.
history: Swabian comfort food since medieval times. Monasteries developed recipe as meatless Friday meal. Regional variations exist across southern Germany.

name: Souvlaki
description: Greek grilled meat skewers with pita, tzatziki, and vegetables.
instructions: Marinate cubed meat in lemon, oil, oregano, garlic.
Thread onto skewers.
Grill over high heat, turning frequently.
Warm pita bread on grill.
Serve wrapped in pita with tzatziki and vegetables.
history: Ancient Greek street food mentioned in Homer's Iliad. Name derives from 'souvla' meaning spit. Remains Greece's most popular fast food.

name: Pastéis de Nata
description: Portuguese custard tarts with flaky pastry and caramelized top.
instructions: Roll puff pastry and line tart molds.
Make custard with egg yolks, sugar, milk, and cream.
Strain custard and pour into pastry shells.
Bake at high temperature until tops are caramelized.
Dust with cinnamon and powdered sugar.
history: Created by Jerónimos Monastery monks in Belém before 1837. Recipe sold to sugar refinery, now Pastéis de Belém remains original secret recipe.
